chapter: Los Angeles: Roy Milton and Central Avenue
title: Roy Milton's standing offer and the union
summary: He sat in with Roy Milton's group at the Cobra Room, and Milton promised a job and union membership.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Previous to that, I had met Roy Milton. I used to go down to the Cobra Room there at First and San Pedro and sit in with them sometimes. Like, Monday nights, on my off night, I'd get around and play with different guys. So Roy Milton, the great Blues singer and drummer, he had his fine group there, with Jose Sep(?) and Camille Howard and Buddy Floyd, the tenor saxophonist, and Cato(?) was the bass player. So Roy told me, he says, "Look, if you ever want to

come back to California, just let me know." He said, "You've got a job." And he said, "And I'll get you in the union, everything." Because he was in tight with the 767, which was the Black local at the time, when they had the segregated local over on Central Avenue. He was Masonic, and most of them were Masonic, so they could pull some deals -- you know, get me in the union. I would have to do the waiting period, which at that time you had to wait three months before you could even take a weekend gig, and then you got to wait three more before you could take a regular gig, you know.
